newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures close lower on weak cash.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures close lower on weak cash.

text.p: Reports of continued weakness in cash markets kept pressure on CME lumber futures and prices finished lower after rising early, traders said.
Lumber closed $4.80 to $2.50 per tbf lower with May up most at $389.30 and July off $4.50 at $384.50 per tbf.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $397 per tbf, unchanged from midweek and $2 under last Friday.

Confusion following word of a bill to reverse the Canadian lumber quota agreement by some congressmen and Canada's saying it was not interested in changing the quota also influenced trade at times, traders said.
"Longer term this is a very important issue for lumber pricing. Short-term it's very difficult to get a handle on," one trader said.
